cases.text: |  |  | Answer review | A police officer signals you to stop while your traffic light is green. What should you do? |  | A. Stop as directed by the officer. | Your answer | Correct answer | A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules. |  | B. Follow the green light | The officer's instruction has higher priority than the light. |  | C. Stop only if there is a stop sign | The police instruction is sufficient. |  | D. Continue if the road looks clear | A clear road does not cancel the instruction. | A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules. | Combine the instructions | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You approach a give-way sign with a clear view and no conflicting traffic. What is required? |  | A. Slow down, check carefully and stop only if necessary. | Your answer | Correct answer | Giving way requires you to avoid obstructing intersecting traffic; a complete stop is not automatic. |  | B. Always stop for five seconds | A give-way sign does not impose a fixed stop. |  | C. Maintain speed because the road is empty | You must clearly demonstrate readiness to yield. |  | D. Give way only to vehicles from the right | The duty covers traffic from both directions. | Giving way requires you to avoid obstructing intersecting traffic; a complete stop is not automatic. | Recognise what a sign asks | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90)

|  |  | Answer review | You reach a stop sign with a marked stop line and no other traffic. Where must you stop? |  | A. Immediately before the stop line. | Your answer | Correct answer | A stop sign requires a complete stop even when the road appears empty. |  | B. Beside the sign regardless of the line | The marked stop line determines the stopping point. |  | C. Only after entering the junction | That puts the car into conflicting traffic. |  | D. There is no need to stop | The stop obligation is unconditional. | A stop sign requires a complete stop even when the road appears empty. | Recognise what a sign asks | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90)

|  |  | Answer review | The car ahead stops at a stop line. You stop behind it. What must you do when you reach the line? |  | A. Make your own complete stop at the line. | Your answer | Correct answer | Each driver must fulfil the stop obligation at the proper stopping point. |  | B. Follow without stopping again | The other driver's stop does not fulfil your obligation. |  | C. Stop only if someone approaches | The obligation applies even without traffic. |  | D. Sound the horn before proceeding | A horn is not a substitute for stopping. | Each driver must fulfil the stop obligation at the proper stopping point. | Recognise what a sign asks | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90)

|  |  | Answer review | Two vehicles meet at an unsigned junction where no other priority rule applies. Who must you give way to? |  | A. Vehicles approaching from your right. | Your answer | Correct answer | The priority-to-the-right rule applies when no sign, signal or other priority rule replaces it. |  | B. Vehicles from the left only | This reverses the rule. |  | C. Only larger vehicles | Vehicle size does not establish priority. |  | D. Nobody if your road is wider | Road width alone does not change the rule. | The priority-to-the-right rule applies when no sign, signal or other priority rule replaces it. | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | A car approaches from your right on a narrower normal road at an otherwise unsigned junction. What applies? |  | A. You give way to it. | Your answer | Correct answer | A wider road is not automatically a priority road. |  | B. The narrower road always gives way | Width alone is not a priority rule. |  | C. You go first if travelling straight | Going straight does not override priority to the right. |  | D. The faster car goes first | Speed never creates priority. | A wider road is not automatically a priority road. | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Two moving cars cross paths inside an open car park, away from parking spaces. No signs regulate priority. What normally applies? |  | A. Give way to the vehicle on your right. | Your answer | Correct answer | Priority to the right can apply in open areas as well as conventional junctions. |  | B. All traffic gives way to the left | That is not the general rule. |  | C. Only painted junctions have priority rules | Markings are not necessary for the rule. |  | D. The first car to sound its horn goes first | A horn cannot establish priority. | Priority to the right can apply in open areas as well as conventional junctions. | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You drive from a house driveway onto a road. What is your obligation? |  | A. Give way to road users whose paths you cross. | Your answer | Correct answer | Leaving a property is covered by the exit rule. |  | B. Give way only to the right | The exit rule is broader than priority to the right. |  | C. Join first if turning right | The turn does not remove the exit obligation. |  | D. Claim priority because you started moving | Starting first does not establish priority. | Leaving a property is covered by the exit rule. | Decide who goes first | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You leave a property across an uninterrupted cycle path before joining the road. What must you do? |  | A. Give way on both the cycle path and the road. | Your answer | Correct answer | The exit rule applies to the path you cross and the road you enter. |  | B. Give way only on the road | Cyclists on the uninterrupted path also have protection. |  | C. Cyclists must always stop for cars | Cars do not have general priority over cyclists. |  | D. Treat the cycle path as a parking strip | It is a route for cyclists, not parking. | The exit rule applies to the path you cross and the road you enter. | Decide who goes first | Turn with a complete picture | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You have a round green light and want to turn left across an oncoming car's path. What applies? |  | A. Let the oncoming car pass before turning. | Your answer | Correct answer | A round green light may also be shown to oncoming traffic; turning duties still apply. |  | B. Green gives you priority in every direction | Green does not cancel the turning rule. |  | C. Turn immediately because you indicated | An indicator communicates intention, not priority. |  | D. The oncoming car must stop for a left turn | It is your turn that crosses its path. | A round green light may also be shown to oncoming traffic; turning duties still apply. | Combine the instructions | Turn with a complete picture | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Your signal turns green, but the road beyond the junction is blocked. What should you do? |  | A. Wait before entering until you can clear the junction. | Your answer | Correct answer | You must avoid becoming stationary where you obstruct crossing traffic. |  | B. Enter because the signal is green | Green does not authorise blocking the junction. |  | C. Stop in the middle to reserve your place | That obstructs other traffic. |  | D. Drive onto the pedestrian crossing and wait | The crossing must also be kept clear. | You must avoid becoming stationary where you obstruct crossing traffic. | Combine the instructions | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | On a road limited to 50 km/h, a bus signals to leave a stop into your lane, the rightmost lane. What must you do? |  | A. Slow down and let the bus leave. | Your answer | Correct answer | At a speed limit of 50 km/h or lower, drivers in the affected lane must allow a signalling bus out. |  | B. Accelerate past before it moves | That frustrates the bus rule. |  | C. The bus always has to wait | The 50 km/h rule applies here. |  | D. Stop in the opposing lane | That introduces a new danger. | At a speed limit of 50 km/h or lower, drivers in the affected lane must allow a signalling bus out. | See the person behind the movement | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | The speed limit is 70 km/h and a bus signals to leave its stop. Which statement is correct? |  | A. The bus must give way, but you should still be ready to cooperate. | Your answer | Correct answer | The special obligation to let a bus out applies at limits of 50 km/h or lower. |  | B. The bus always has unconditional priority | The limit is above the bus-rule threshold. |  | C. You should block the bus deliberately | All drivers still owe care and consideration. |  | D. The bus may pull out without looking | Its driver must avoid danger. | The special obligation to let a bus out applies at limits of 50 km/h or lower. | See the person behind the movement | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | A light changes from green to amber and you can stop safely before the line. What must you do? |  | A. Stop before the line. | Your answer | Correct answer | Amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping safely is no longer possible. |  | B. Accelerate to beat red | Amber is not an invitation to speed up. |  | C. Continue whenever the junction is empty | An empty junction does not remove the stop requirement. |  | D. Wait until red before braking | That can make the stop unsafe or too late. | Amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping safely is no longer possible. | Combine the instructions | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90) | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Traffic signals are flashing amber. How do you determine priority? |  | A. Use the applicable signs or general priority rules with extra caution. | Your answer | Correct answer | Flashing amber warns that normal signal control is not operating. |  | B. Treat it as a permanent green light | It grants no general right to proceed. |  | C. Treat every approach as a priority road | Priority must come from signs or rules. |  | D. Ignore pedestrians until signals recover | Pedestrian duties still apply. | Flashing amber warns that normal signal control is not operating. | Combine the instructions | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90) | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Your traffic signal displays red and amber together. What does it mean? |  | A. Remain stopped; green is about to appear. | Your answer | Correct answer | The combined signal still requires you to stop. |  | B. Start moving across the line | The signal has not yet permitted movement. |  | C. Proceed if turning right | There is no general right turn on red. |  | D. Only pedestrians must wait | The signal applies to the drivers facing it. | The combined signal still requires you to stop. | Combine the instructions | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90) | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | A pedestrian is about to enter an uncontrolled crossing. What should you do? |  | A. Clearly slow down and give way. | Your answer | Correct answer | Drivers must give way to pedestrians on or about to enter an uncontrolled crossing. |  | B. Continue until the pedestrian steps into your lane | The duty begins before they reach your lane. |  | C. Sound the horn to make them wait | A horn does not replace giving way. |  | D. Give way only to children | The crossing rule protects all pedestrians. | Drivers must give way to pedestrians on or about to enter an uncontrolled crossing. | Crossings belong to people | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Cykelpassage och cykelöverfart - Transportstyrelsen | Övergångsställe - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | A person pushes a bicycle over a pedestrian crossing. How are they treated? |  | A. As a pedestrian. | Your answer | Correct answer | A person walking with a bicycle is a pedestrian rather than a riding cyclist. |  | B. As a motor vehicle | A pushed bicycle is not a motor vehicle. |  | C. As a cyclist who is riding | They are walking rather than riding. |  | D. As someone prohibited from crossing | Pushing a bicycle is allowed. | A person walking with a bicycle is a pedestrian rather than a riding cyclist. | Crossings belong to people | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Cykelpassage och cykelöverfart - Transportstyrelsen | Övergångsställe - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | You drive straight towards an uncontrolled bicycle passage. Which duty applies to you? |  | A. Adapt speed so you do not endanger cyclists already on the passage. | Your answer | Correct answer | The cyclist's obligation to give way does not remove the driver's duty to avoid danger. |  | B. Maintain speed regardless of cyclists | Drivers still have a safety obligation. |  | C. Treat it as an automatic green signal | No signal is present. |  | D. Accelerate to force cyclists to stop | Deliberately creating danger is unacceptable. | The cyclist's obligation to give way does not remove the driver's duty to avoid danger. | Crossings belong to people | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Cykelpassage och cykelöverfart - Transportstyrelsen | Övergångsställe - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | You turn across an uncontrolled bicycle passage. A cyclist is about to enter it. What should you do? |  | A. Drive slowly and give the cyclist an opportunity to pass. | Your answer | Correct answer | Turning drivers and drivers exiting a roundabout have additional duties at bicycle passages. |  | B. Use your indicator to force the cyclist to wait | Indicating does not remove the obligation. |  | C. Apply only the straight-road situation | The turning situation has additional duties. |  | D. Stop on the passage to block it | That obstructs the cyclist's route. | Turning drivers and drivers exiting a roundabout have additional duties at bicycle passages. | Crossings belong to people | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Cykelpassage och cykelöverfart - Transportstyrelsen | Övergångsställe - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | A signed bicycle crossing has the prescribed markings. A cyclist is about to use it. What applies? |  | A. You must give way to the cyclist. | Your answer | Correct answer | A bicycle crossing has an explicit driver duty to yield to cyclists using or about to use it. |  | B. Cyclists always yield because they are smaller | Vehicle size does not establish priority. |  | C. The rule applies only to pedestrians | This is a bicycle crossing. |  | D. The cyclist must dismount first | Dismounting is not required at a bicycle crossing. | A bicycle crossing has an explicit driver duty to yield to cyclists using or about to use it. | Crossings belong to people | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 | Cykelpassage och cykelöverfart - Transportstyrelsen | Övergångsställe - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | You approach a signed roundabout. Who must you give way to? |  | A. All vehicles already circulating in it. | Your answer | Correct answer | The entry obligation applies to circulating vehicles, including bicycles. |  | B. Only vehicles from your right | Roundabout entry has its own rule. |  | C. Only motor vehicles | Bicycles are vehicles too. |  | D. Nobody if you are taking the first exit | Your intended exit does not remove the duty. | The entry obligation applies to circulating vehicles, including bicycles. | Choose a safe path through a roundabout | Att köra i cirkulationsplats | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Which signal is required when leaving a roundabout? |  | A. Indicate right. | Your answer | Correct answer | An exit is a movement to the right and must be signalled. |  | B. Indicate left until fully outside | That gives the wrong exit message. |  | C. Use hazard warning lights | Hazard lights do not indicate a normal exit. |  | D. No signal if travelling straight overall | You still need to signal the exit. | An exit is a movement to the right and must be signalled. | Choose a safe path through a roundabout | Att köra i cirkulationsplats | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You are in an inner roundabout lane and want to cross the outer lane to exit. What must you do? |  | A. Check and change lanes only without danger or obstruction. | Your answer | Correct answer | Being in the inner lane does not give priority over traffic in the outer lane. |  | B. Force outer-lane traffic to stop | Lane changes must be safe. |  | C. Exit immediately whenever you indicate | Indicating does not create a gap. |  | D. Stop abruptly in the circulating lane | An abrupt stop can cause a collision; continue around if needed. | Being in the inner lane does not give priority over traffic in the outer lane. | Choose a safe path through a roundabout | Att köra i cirkulationsplats | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | May you make a voluntary stop in a road tunnel to check directions? |  | A. No; continue to a suitable permitted stopping place. | Your answer | Correct answer | Voluntary stopping and parking in a tunnel are prohibited. |  | B. Yes with hazard lights | Hazard lights do not legalise a voluntary stop. |  | C. Yes for less than one minute | Duration does not create an exception. |  | D. Yes if the engine stays on | Engine status does not change the restriction. | Voluntary stopping and parking in a tunnel are prohibited. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You want to park 6 metres before a pedestrian crossing. Is this permitted? |  | A. No, stopping and parking are prohibited within 10 metres before it. | Your answer | Correct answer | A vehicle there can hide pedestrians from approaching drivers. |  | B. Yes if you remain in the car | Remaining inside does not remove the prohibition. |  | C. Yes if the crossing is empty | The distance rule still applies. |  | D. Yes if the car is small | Vehicle size does not remove the rule. | A vehicle there can hide pedestrians from approaching drivers. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You wait at the roadside for a friend who is still inside a building. What is this normally classed as? |  | A. Parking. | Your answer | Correct answer | Waiting is parking when no actual boarding, alighting, loading or unloading is taking place. |  | B. Always loading | Waiting for a person is not loading goods. |  | C. Never parking if the engine runs | A running engine does not change the definition. |  | D. A traffic-required stop | The traffic situation did not require you to wait. | Waiting is parking when no actual boarding, alighting, loading or unloading is taking place. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | May you park on a priority road where there is no sign permitting parking? |  | A. No. | Your answer | Correct answer | Parking on a priority road is generally prohibited unless parking is specifically permitted. |  | B. Yes whenever there is a hard shoulder | A shoulder alone is not permission. |  | C. Yes for 24 hours | The ordinary parking time rule does not override this prohibition. |  | D. Yes with parking lights | Lights improve visibility but do not create permission. | Parking on a priority road is generally prohibited unless parking is specifically permitted. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You want to park 20 metres from a railway crossing. What applies? |  | A. Parking is prohibited within 30 metres of the crossing. | Your answer | Correct answer | The parking restriction extends 30 metres on either side of a railway or tramway crossing. |  | B. Parking is prohibited only on the rails | The restriction extends beyond the rails. |  | C. Parking is allowed if no train is visible | Train visibility does not change the distance rule. |  | D. Only large vehicles are prohibited | The restriction also applies to cars. | The parking restriction extends 30 metres on either side of a railway or tramway crossing. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | On which side may you park on a one-way street, if signs and other rules permit? |  | A. Either side. | Your answer | Correct answer | One-way streets are an exception to the usual right-side stopping and parking rule. |  | B. Only on the right in all cases | One-way streets allow the left side too. |  | C. Only in the middle | Parking in the middle would obstruct traffic. |  | D. On the pavement | One-way status does not permit pavement parking. | One-way streets are an exception to the usual right-side stopping and parking rule. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Date parking applies today, an even-numbered date. Which side is prohibited? |  | A. The side with even house numbers. | Your answer | Correct answer | During the restriction's hours, the date and prohibited side have the same parity. |  | B. The side with odd numbers | That reverses the date-parking rule. |  | C. Both sides all day | Check the sign's times; the rule identifies one side. |  | D. Neither side on even dates | Even dates are covered by the rule. | During the restriction's hours, the date and prohibited side have the same parity. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90) | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | What do times in parentheses on a parking panel normally refer to? |  | A. Weekdays before Sundays and public holidays. | Your answer | Correct answer | Parentheses mean weekdays before Sundays and public holidays, including relevant holiday eves; they do not include a Sunday merely because it precedes a holiday. |  | B. Only Sundays | Sundays and public holidays normally use red times. |  | C. Every weekday | Ordinary weekday times are shown without parentheses. |  | D. Only school holidays | School holidays do not define these times. | Parenthesised times apply on weekdays before Sundays and public holidays. Sundays and public holidays use the red times; a named day can override the usual category. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Vägmärkesförordning (2007:90) | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen

|  |  | Answer review | At an unmarked bus stop, where does the stopping restriction normally extend? |  | A. 20 metres before and 5 metres after the stop sign. | Your answer | Correct answer | The larger approach space allows a bus to enter its stop. |  | B. 5 metres before and 20 after | That reverses the distances. |  | C. Exactly 10 metres on both sides | Those are not the bus-stop distances. |  | D. Only directly beside the sign | The protected area extends beyond the sign. | The larger approach space allows a bus to enter its stop. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | May you briefly pick up a passenger at a bus stop? |  | A. Only if you do not hinder bus or tram traffic. | Your answer | Correct answer | Actual boarding and alighting may be allowed, but the stop must remain usable by public transport. |  | B. Yes even if a bus must wait | You must not hinder the bus. |  | C. Only if you are also unloading furniture | Goods unloading is not the passenger exception. |  | D. Never under any circumstances | A limited passenger exception exists. | Actual boarding and alighting may be allowed, but the stop must remain usable by public transport. | Choose a lawful place to stop | Stanna och parkera - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You miss your motorway exit. What should you do? |  | A. Continue to the next suitable exit. | Your answer | Correct answer | Reversing or turning around on a motorway is prohibited. |  | B. Reverse along the shoulder | Reversing is prohibited even on the shoulder. |  | C. Use an opening in the central barrier | Such openings are not for ordinary U-turns. |  | D. Stop and walk back to the exit | Stopping and walking on the motorway are not permitted for this purpose. | Reversing or turning around on a motorway is prohibited. | Join faster traffic calmly | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You join a motorway using an acceleration lane. What approach is correct? |  | A. Adapt your speed and cooperate with traffic to merge safely. | Your answer | Correct answer | Both entering and existing traffic must show consideration and adapt. |  | B. Entering traffic has absolute priority | The lane does not grant absolute priority. |  | C. Motorway traffic must always stop | Stopping is not the normal merging method. |  | D. Merge without checking the blind spot | Mirrors alone can miss nearby vehicles. | Both entering and existing traffic must show consideration and adapt. | Join faster traffic calmly | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | May a class I moped use a motorway because it can travel at 45 km/h? |  | A. No, mopeds are prohibited. | Your answer | Correct answer | The design-speed requirement does not override the specific ban on mopeds. |  | B. Yes because 45 is above 40 | Mopeds are explicitly excluded. |  | C. Yes on the shoulder only | The shoulder is not a moped route. |  | D. Yes if the driver holds a B licence | The vehicle prohibition still applies. | The design-speed requirement does not override the specific ban on mopeds. | Join faster traffic calmly | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | On a normal two-way road, may you overtake a car immediately before an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing? |  | A. No. | Your answer | Correct answer | Overtaking there can hide pedestrians and is prohibited. |  | B. Yes if you sound the horn | A horn does not create an exception. |  | C. Yes if the car is slow | Its speed does not remove the prohibition. |  | D. Yes if the centre line is broken | A broken line does not override the crossing restriction. | Overtaking there can hide pedestrians and is prohibited. | Is passing worth the risk? | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | May you exceed the posted speed limit briefly to finish overtaking? |  | A. No. | Your answer | Correct answer | The speed limit still applies during an overtake. |  | B. Yes by up to 10 km/h | There is no general overtaking allowance. |  | C. Yes for less than five seconds | Duration does not legalise speeding. |  | D. Yes if the other driver agrees | Another driver's agreement cannot change the limit. | The speed limit still applies during an overtake. | Is passing worth the risk? | Leave room to respond | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | A train approaches, but the railway crossing's red lights are not flashing. What must you do? |  | A. Give way to the train. | Your answer | Correct answer | You must check for trains and yield even if warning equipment is not operating. |  | B. Cross because the red light is off | The absence of a red signal is not a guarantee. |  | C. Sound your horn and cross | A train cannot readily stop or swerve. |  | D. Expect the train to give way | Road vehicles yield to trains. | You must check for trains and yield even if warning equipment is not operating. | Expect an interrupted route | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | The traffic beyond a railway crossing has stopped, leaving no room for your car. What should you do? |  | A. Wait before the crossing until your whole vehicle can clear it. | Your answer | Correct answer | Never enter a crossing if you risk stopping on the tracks. |  | B. Enter while the barriers are open | Open barriers do not make the space beyond sufficient. |  | C. Stop with only the rear over the rails | Any part of the car on the track is dangerous. |  | D. Follow closely to claim the gap | That can trap your car on the crossing. | Never enter a crossing if you risk stopping on the tracks. | Expect an interrupted route | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | A signed home zone appears empty. How fast may you drive? |  | A. At walking speed. | Your answer | Correct answer | The walking-speed rule applies even when no pedestrian is visible. |  | B. At 30 km/h | A home zone is not an ordinary 30 zone. |  | C. At 50 km/h | The home-zone rule replaces the ordinary limit. |  | D. As fast as visibility allows | Walking speed remains the maximum. | The walking-speed rule applies even when no pedestrian is visible. | When the street changes purpose | Gågata, cykelgata och gångfartsområde - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | You drive on a signed bicycle street. What speed rule applies? |  | A. Adapt to cyclists and never exceed 30 km/h. | Your answer | Correct answer | The maximum is 30 km/h, but cyclists may require a lower speed. |  | B. Always drive exactly 30 km/h | Adaptation may require a much lower speed. |  | C. Walking speed in every case | That is the home-zone rule, not the bicycle-street maximum. |  | D. 50 km/h when cyclists are absent | The 30 km/h maximum still applies. | The maximum is 30 km/h, but cyclists may require a lower speed. | When the street changes purpose | Gågata, cykelgata och gångfartsområde - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | May you use a pedestrian street as a convenient through route in your car? |  | A. No, ordinary through driving is not an authorised purpose. | Your answer | Correct answer | Only specified essential access is allowed, such as certain deliveries or access to homes. |  | B. Yes if you drive at walking speed | Speed compliance alone does not authorise access. |  | C. Yes if there are no pedestrians | Absence of pedestrians does not permit through driving. |  | D. Yes after dark | The access restriction does not disappear at night. | Only specified essential access is allowed, such as certain deliveries or access to homes. | When the street changes purpose | Gågata, cykelgata och gångfartsområde - Transportstyrelsen | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | When driving an ordinary passenger car on the road, may you use dipped headlights and front fog lights together? |  | A. No. | Your answer | Correct answer | For the passenger car specified here, the combination is prohibited. Do not generalise this answer to the separate daylight-motorcycle exception. |  | B. Yes in all darkness | Darkness does not permit that combination. |  | C. Yes if your car is new | Vehicle age does not change the rule. |  | D. Yes when overtaking | Overtaking creates no lighting exception. | For this car, use the permitted lighting for visibility; dipped headlights and front fog lights must not be used together. The separate daylight-motorcycle exception is outside this scenario. | Drive within what you can see | Choose the right vehicle lighting

|  |  | Answer review | A priority road bends right at a junction and you follow it. Must you indicate the turn? |  | A. Yes, signal your change of direction. | Your answer | Correct answer | Priority does not replace communicating your intention to turn. |  | B. No because you remain on the priority road | The direction change still needs signalling. |  | C. Only if leaving the priority road | It is the manoeuvre that matters. |  | D. Use the left indicator | That communicates the opposite direction. | Priority does not replace communicating your intention to turn. | Move with control | Turn with a complete picture | Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1

|  |  | Answer review | Which way of studying driving theory is most likely to build lasting understanding? |  | A. Understanding why rules exist and applying them to new situations. | Your answer | Correct answer | Deep learning connects rules to their purpose, helping you handle unfamiliar situations. |  | B. Memorising only the answer letters | Letters can change and do not teach the rule. |  | C. Skipping explanations after correct answers | You may miss the reasoning needed in a different situation. |  | D. Learning only the easiest questions | That leaves important gaps in knowledge. | Deep learning connects rules to their purpose, helping you handle unfamiliar situations. | Make a realistic readiness plan | Category B syllabus, chapter 5 | Trafikverket: safety check

|  |  | Answer review | Why should basic vehicle controls become well practised? |  | A.
